To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the phase retrieval problem is equivalent to recovering a rank 1 positive semi-definite (PSD), low rank matrix, and (b) the phase retrieval algorithm is stable with respect to noise and over-sampling.

(1) the phase retrieval problem can be formulated as the problem of recovering a low rank PSD matrix from its Fourier measurements; (2) this problem can be solved by a non convex algorithm based on matrix completion; (3) the stability of the inverse problem depends on the oversampling rate.
we provide a new algorithm to solve the phase retrieval problem based on matrix completion and we provide theory on how oversampling affects this problem.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase retrieval problem is stable in the low rank regime, even if the number of measurements is smaller than the ambient dimension of the signal.

the lifted problem is stable in the sense of the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP) and that the number of samples required for stability scales with the rank $K$, and is independent of the dimension of the original problem.
the stability of the inverse problem is not determined by the number of samples $n$, but by the number of non zero singular values in $A$ which is determined by the rank and oversampling.
